7
A device for spraying paint consists of a box with its faces horizontal and vertical. One of its
vertical faces contains small holes. Paint is fed into the box under pressure via a vertical tube and
exits through the holes as fine streams moving horizontally.
paint in
paint out through holes
(only a few holes are shown)
The paint is ejected at a speed of 2.5 m s–1 through 400 holes, each of area 0.4 mm2. The density
of the paint is 900 kg m–3.
What is the horizontal force required to hold the device stationary as it ejects the paint?
A
0.36 N
B
0.90 N
C
2.3 N
D
900 N

hints: Notice the paint gains horizontal momentum: it enters vertically but leaves horizontally at $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ through 400 holes.
Connect holding force to rate of change of momentum using $F = (\text{mass per second}) \times (\text{change in velocity})$.
First find total exit area in $\text{m}^2$ from $400 \times 0.4 \text{ mm}^2$, then volume per second $Av$, then mass per second $\rho Av$.
walkthrough: Find the total area for the paint to leave: $A = 400 \times 0.4 \text{ mm}^2 = 160 \text{ mm}^2$. Convert to $\text{m}^2$: $A = 160 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2 = 1.6 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$.
Find the volume ejected per second: volume per second $= Av = 1.6 \times 10^{-4} \times 2.5 = 4.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$.
Find the mass ejected per second using density $\rho = 900 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$: mass per second $= \rho Av = 900 \times 4.0 \times 10^{-4} = 0.36 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$.
Apply Newton's second law as rate of change of momentum. Each kilogram gains horizontal velocity $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $F = 0.36 \times 2.5 = 0.90 \text{ N}$.
This holding force must act opposite to the paint jets to keep horizontal momentum balanced. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is the mass ejected per second in $\text{kg s}^{-1}$, not the force. It must still be multiplied by the change in horizontal velocity.

B.explanation: Mass per second times ejection speed gives $0.36 \times 2.5 = 0.90 \text{ N}$, equal to the rate of gain of horizontal momentum.

C.explanation: This value is too large and does not follow from $\rho A v^2$ when the total hole area is converted correctly from $\text{mm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$.

D.explanation: This uses the density $900 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ as if it were a force and ignores volume flow rate and ejection speed.
